paragraphs: On Tuesday, Lily, Mia, and Leo sat on the steps of the school stage. The hall was big, and the stage had three wooden steps. They planned a small show for the Explorers. "The show is on Thursday at two o'clock," said Lily. "Teacher Kim wants a snack for the children." "What can we bring?" asked Leo.

"I can bring yogurt," said Mia. "My mom has four big boxes at home." "Then we need small bowls and spoons," said Lily. "I can ask Teacher Kim," said Mia. "She has twenty bowls in the library." "Good," said Lily. "Leo, what can you bring?"

"I can bring bananas," said Leo. Leo eats one banana every morning, so he knows a lot about them. "There are two trees in our garden, so we have a lot." "Can you cut them?" asked Mia. "Yes, I can," said Leo. "But I need a fork, because the bananas are soft." "Does the school have forks?" asked Lily. "The cook has some," said Mia. "I can follow her to the kitchen after lunch."

"What about you, Lily?" asked Leo. "I will make the sign for the table," said Lily. "It says, 'Snacks for the Explorers.'" "And I will prepare the table on Thursday morning." "Where do we put the snacks?" asked Mia. "On the long table next to the stage," said Lily. "The children can take a bowl after the show." "This is not a big meal, but it is a good snack," said Leo.

Teacher Kim came to the stage with a notebook. She looked at the plan and nodded. "Are you ready?" she asked. "Yes," said Lily. "Mia brings yogurt, Leo brings bananas, and I make the sign." "Excellent," said Teacher Kim. "I will bring the bowls and the spoons on Thursday." Leo wrote the list on his hand with a pen, and the girls laughed.
